title.narrative: Sindh Union Council and Community Economic Strengthening Support (SUCCESS) ¿ RSPN component

description.narrative: The objectives of the RSPN role in the SUCCESS programme are to complement implementation of the programme by partner RSPs, by ensuring effective quality control, standardisation, documentation and responsiveness to lessons learnt, by fostering and maintaining a component of research and knowledge management, and by providing value-added strategic support such as development of common implementation methodologies and processes.

title.narrative: 1.Percentage of the households with PSC 023

description.narrative: 1.Percentage of the households with PSC 023

comment.narrative: In the logframe the baseline data of 56 is taken from the PSC census done at the start of the programme. However to measure this indicator we have later conducted a sample baseline survey and sample endline survey. Here we have used the baseline and endline survey data to measure this indicator.According to the endline survey 2022 estimated that 25 of the households in the poor PSC 023 category moved up to the nonpoor category between 2016 and 2022.However there was no change in the overall poverty status in the programme area as estimated by the PSC Out of the 1833 households sampled in the survey 464 in the poor category moved up to the nonpoor PSC 24100 category while approximately the same number of nonpoor households 459 moved into the poor category. The wellbeing of some of the poor as well as the nonpoor was affected adversely during the programme implementation period The 459 households that moved from the nonpoor to the poor category between the baseline and the endline constituted 47 of the nonpoor in the sample.The key factors that mattered included macroeconomic policies the stabilisation programme agreed with the International Monetary Fund in July 2019 the lockdowns associated with the COVID19 pandemic since March 2020 and natural disasters.

description.narrative: 1.1.Percentage of project outcomes are achieved by RSPs:a.Percent of technically and financially viable women led (COs/VOs/LSOs) Scoring 70% or above on the Institutional Maturity Index. b.Percentage of women CIF and IGG beneficiaries investing in income generating activities and livelihood assetsc.Percent of women and men (TVST beneficiaries) employed in formal and informal sectors and/or in micro business.d.Percent change in health expenditure of MHI users. e.Percentage of implemented community physical infrastructure schemes operated and maintained by communities.f.Percentage of targeted poor households (poverty score of 0 23) which have:(i)CNIC(ii)Schoolaged children going to school(iii)Eligible children vaccinated(iv)Consulted public health facility at time of illness/injury(v)Access to improved drinking water sources (piped water or hand pump in dwelling)(vi)Latrine in the house(vii)Drainage for water disposal from housesg.Percent of women adult literacy learners able to read and write simple sentences in Sindhi/Urdu and perform twodigit numeric operations of plus, minus and multiplication.

comment.narrative: The reported achievement is an average of all the values mentioned in the description above. The target of 70 is overachieved.
